chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wasshash, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever finds the coolness of our love in his liver (heart), let him praise God for the first blessing." I said, "May I be your ransom, what is the first blessing?" He said, "The purity of lineage."

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, "The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Fatimah (peace be upon her), 'Make permissible for the fathers of our Shias their share from the Fay (booty/gains), so that they may be pleased.'
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'We have made permissible for the mothers of our Shias [marriage to] their fathers, so that they may be pleased.'

key_terms.بَرْدُ الْحُبِّ: Coolness of love (metaphor for deep affection)
key_terms.لِيَطِيبُوا: So that they may be pleased

ai.seo_question: What is considered the first blessing in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the 'first blessing' as the coolness of love for the Ahl al-Bayt in one's heart, linked to the purity of lineage. The narration further cites Imam Ali (peace be upon him) instructing Fatimah (peace be upon her) to allow the fathers of their Shia to marry their mothers from the spoils of war (Fay), a ruling extended by the Imams to facilitate family reunification and please the believers. This specific legal dispensation highlights the unique status of the Shia's familial bonds with the Prophet's household, distinguishing them within the broader community of believers.
